models.name: 1X World Model
models.summary: Models and data from the 1X World Model Challenge, which asks a model to predict the first-person camera view of 1X's EVE humanoid robot from its past frames and actions. The release includes small Genie-style baselines and a tokenizer; it is a research benchmark rather than an interactive app.
models.controls: Robot action and video modeling
controlsDetail: Past camera frames from the robot
The robot's action data for each step
models.licenseNote: The selected weight model card declares this license. Check the license text, dependencies and intended use before adoption.
howToRun: Install the repository's dependencies and download the challenge data.
Generate frames with genie/generate.py and the 1x-technologies/GENIE_138M checkpoint, then view them with visualize.py.
Score the results with genie/evaluate.py.
models.measurement: Not independently measured for this directory

models.name: Echo-Memory
models.summary: An action-conditioned world model study from JD that compares four kinds of memory for keeping a generated scene consistent when the camera leaves and comes back. It is built on Wan 2.1 1.3B and released with code, checkpoints and ComfyUI nodes under CC BY 4.0.

controlsDetail: A first frame to start from
Camera actions for each chunk of video

Point the inference script at the base model and a first frame, then generate the video chunk by chunk with camera actions.
ComfyUI users can install the project's custom nodes (loader, camera action, generate) from its comfyui folder or the Comfy Registry.

models.name: EdenLive
models.summary: EdenLive is a generative renderer: you feed it a rough source video, such as game footage or a live camera, plus a scene prompt and a reference image, and it re-renders each chunk as a new world while keeping the source motion. Movement comes from the source video, not from direct keyboard commands.
models.controls: Source video (game footage or a live camera), a scene prompt and a reference image
controlsDetail: A source video: game footage or a live camera
models.licenseNote: The video pipeline's weights are Apache-2.0, with an MIT CLIP encoder and a vision encoder under Meta's DINOv3 License. The optional first-frame workbench uses FLUX.2 [klein] under a non-commercial license.
models.realtimeDetail: 24 fps or higher at 480p or 720p, minute-scale generation.
howToRun: Clone VAST-AI-Research/EdenLive, create a Python 3.10 conda environment, and install PyTorch and the pinned packages from the README.
Download VAST-AI/EdenLive from Hugging Face.
For offline clips, run python -m edenlive.scripts.infer.
For the live service, start the TURN relay (bash turn_server.sh), then the model service (bash start.sh 14b, or 5b).

models.name: Neural World Models
models.summary: Navigation World Models predict what a robot's camera will see after a navigation action, and can plan a route by imagining trajectories before taking them. Code and weights are for non-commercial use.
models.controls: Navigation action conditioning
models.licenseNote: Hugging Face metadata says CC BY 4.0, but the project README licenses code and weights under CC BY-NC 4.0. The stricter, non-commercial reading is shown.
howToRun: Clone facebookresearch/nwm and install the packages listed in the README.
Download the pretrained model.
Use isolated_nwm_infer.py to predict the next view after an action or to follow a recorded trajectory, and isolated_nwm_eval.py to score the results.
models.measurement: Not independently measured for this directory

Download the tokenizer and world model checkpoints from Hugging Face and place them in the experiment folders.

models.name: Zing
models.summary: Zing-0.5 is a 5B causal world model that keeps rolling a scene forward while keyboard actions and text prompts change it mid-stream. It starts from text or a single image, and the weights are Apache-2.0.
models.controls: W/A/S/D/I/J/K/L keys and text prompts during a rollout
models.licenseNote: The selected weight model card declares this license. Check the license text, dependencies and intended use before adoption.
models.realtimeDetail: Real-time interaction; outputs 24 fps video.
howToRun: Run bash run.sh with a messages file of prompts and actions; ready-made examples cover text-started, image-started and prompt-switched rollouts.
To serve it, launch it with SGLang and drive it from examples/zing_0_5/client.py.
Sliding-window options (--local-attn-size and --sink-size) set how much past video the model attends to.
